subject: Post-call: Multilingual evals & recommended models for EU/APAC locales
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@globexretail.com>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@globexretail.co.jp>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — multilingual evals (EU/APAC)

Hi Lucie / Kenji —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we agreed on: 

Scope & goals:
- Primary use case: product Q&A and localized help articles for FR/DE/ES (EU) and JA/KO/VI (APAC).
- Success metrics: accuracy / helpfulness (human-eval benchmarks), hallucination rate <5% on slot-filling tasks, and latency target <=200ms for short prompts in EU; APAC goal <=250ms if served from Tokyo.
- Volume: ~2M requests/month expected, bursty during promotions.
- Compliance: EU data residency requirement for EU customer content; SOC 2 + contractual DPA required.

Recommended immediate next steps (we'll own items 1-3):
1) Deliver preliminary eval report with recommended model family and localized prompt sets (ETA: 48 business hours).
2) Provision an eval sandbox in EU and APAC (Tokyo) with sample subset from your QA team for 1-week runs.
3) Share model-level benchmarks and suggested quantization/profile options to meet latency targets.

Preliminary model recommendations (subject to eval results):
- redwood-titan-xl (quantized): strong balance of accuracy + low latency in EU; good for FR/DE/ES.
- open-mistral-7b-instruct (LLM-7B-quant): lightweight option for high-throughput endpoints.
- custom eu-tuned variant (we can surface a .pt quantized build) for domain safety/regulatory needs.

I attached the evaluation plan and prompt-set outline we'll use. I'll follow up with the sandbox invite and the Drive link to the benchmark dashboards.

Thanks - will schedule a 30m walkthrough once you have the sandbox data uploaded.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112
[Attachment: eval_plan_globex_multilingual.pdf (pdf, 320KB)]

From: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@globexretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@globexretail.co.jp>, QA Team <qa@globexretail.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — multilingual evals (EU/APAC)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of quick clarifications before you start the sandbox: 
- For EU languages, we need tests on both product descriptions and returns/fraud-related queries (sensitive phrasing). Were those in scope for the prompt sets?
- For JA/KO, we have short-text product Q&A and longer explanation pages — can you confirm the sample sizes you need for each?
- Do your hallucination metrics include entity hallucination (e.g., inventing SKUs)? That's one of our main concerns.

If you can confirm those points and share the Drive link, we can get our QA team to trim and upload a 2k sample per locale by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Lucie
Head of AI Ops, Globex Retail
lucie.dubois@globexretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@globexretail.com>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@globexretail.co.jp>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — multilingual evals (EU/APAC)

Thanks Lucie - yes, good questions. Short answers: 
- Scope: prompt_set_globex_v2.csv includes separate buckets for (a) product descriptions, (b) returns/fraud phrased queries, and (c) help-article summarization. We'll annotate sensitivity for each item.
- Sample sizes: for initial evals 2k examples per high-priority locale (FR/DE/ES/JA/KO) is ideal; for long-form docs ~500 examples per locale.
- Hallucination metrics: we compute entity hallucination separately (precision on recognized SKUs/attributes) and include span-level F1 + human spot checks in the dashboard.

I've attached the preliminary eval report and the prompt set CSV. Also sharing the Drive folder with the benchmark dashboards and the HubSpot deal link.

Attachments: redwood_eval_report_v1.pdf, prompt_set_globex_v2.csv
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_eval_globex_multilingual
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/GLOBEX-1973

Proposed next call: Thursday 19 Feb, 10:00 CET for a 30m walkthrough (will cover results, model tradeoffs, and recommended canary rollout). Can you confirm?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_eval_report_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@globexretail.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & next steps — multilingual evals (EU/APAC)

Heads up / technical notes for the eval sandbox: 
- Tokenization differences: Japanese and Korean tokenizers will produce different token counts which affects per-token latency and cost estimates - we'll normalize metrics to input-character buckets for fairness.
- Locale-specific prompts: suggest using localized templates (we have ready translations + culturally-aware phrasing) rather than literal translations to reduce regression. I'll include an initial set in the sandbox.
- Latency note: with redwood-titan-xl quantized in Tokyo region we see median p95 ~140-180ms for short prompts on Dedicated pools; hosted may be 20-40ms higher depending on regional egress.
- Evaluation: we'll include automated hallucination checks (SKU/price consistency) + a 200-sample human-eval slice per locale to sanity-check automated signals.

I'll upload tokenizer mappings and the localized prompt templates to the Drive folder by EOD.

-Rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Rishi -

Tokyo region for APAC is preferred. A few asks from our side: 
1) Please confirm that EU-origin content will stay in EU sandbox (we require data residency during eval).
2) We'll upload an initial sample (globex_product_qa_ja_sample.json) - it contains synthetic-ish product Q&A with real SKUs redacted. Please let me know the preferred upload method (Drive link or SFTP).
3) Can you expose the model variant names and the quantization profile used for each benchmark run so we can map regressions back to specific builds?

We are OK for the 19 Feb call; Lucie will confirm the exact time.

Best,
Kenji

Hi all - quick update and confirmed next steps: 

1) Sandbox provisioning: we'll spin up 2 isolated sandboxes - one EU (Frankfurt) and one APAC (Tokyo). EU content will remain in the EU sandbox; we will not replicate EU-origin data to APAC.
2) Upload method: please use the Drive folder first (link below). If you prefer SFTP for larger dumps, we can provide a temporary credential.
3) Variant tracking: every benchmark run will include a run_id and explicit model/quant profile metadata in the results CSV so you can trace regressions back to artifacts.
4) Timeline: sandbox ready by 19 Feb EOD CET; initial 1-week run starts 20 Feb.

Action items assigned:
- Globex QA: upload 2k per locale by EOD Fri 13 Feb (Kenji / Lucie) - received JA sample, remaining uploads pending.
- Redwood SE (Rishi): upload tokenizer mappings + localized prompt templates (ETA: 12 Feb) - in progress.
- Redwood AM (Marissa): schedule 30m walkthrough on 19 Feb and share invite.

I'll send the calendar invite after Lucie confirms the time. If you need an NDA/DPA signature faster, loop in legal and we'll prioritize.
